rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun, moon, night, and day obey fixed paths and timing, showing that the Creator alone controls the universe; rival administrators would clash and destroy it, while worshipped celestial bodies are especially subject to His authority.
rows.anchor: the reins of everything are in the hands of the all-powerful and almighty God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “they” in “their generation” refers to the addressees as human beings.
rows.anchor: refers to the addressees in their capacity of human beings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word dhurriyyah means a generation.
rows.anchor: The word َّیِّرُذٌة refers to “a generation.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mashhūn is used for a laden ship.
rows.anchor: The word ونُحْشَم is used for a laden ship.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea’s ability to carry generations of people in ships loaded with thousands of tons, without drowning them, is a sign of God’s care.
rows.anchor: God for the sea travel of generations of mankind has made sea water capable of lifting ships laden with thousands of tons

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made land transport analogous to ships, including horses and camels; Arabs called the camel the ship of the desert.
rows.anchor: These include horses and camels. In particular, the camel was regarded by the Arabs as the ship of the desert.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also covers later technological transport, including cars, lorries, buses, and airplanes.
rows.anchor: technology has invented today like cars, lorries, buses and airplanes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made and taught the scientific laws governing transport; people invent and benefit by applying those laws.
rows.anchor: The laws of science which govern the working of these things have been made and taught by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verse’s transport is God’s gift and mercy: ships laden with goods safely run across sea waters.
rows.anchor: it is God’s mercy that their ships laden with goods and merchandise run about on sea waters

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarīkh can mean pleading, answering a plea, a person who pleads, or a person who answers; all senses suit the verse.
rows.anchor: means “to plead” and “to answer pleadings” as well as “one who pleads”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships’ safe passage is God’s mercy; if He wills, He can drown them and their passengers, who then cannot plead, find an answer, or escape destruction.
rows.anchor: it is God’s mercy that their ships laden with goods and merchandise run about on sea waters

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human favors are gifts of God’s graciousness, not ancestral inheritance or products of human power and ability.
rows.anchor: whatever favours man has is neither a legacy of his forefathers nor the result of his power and ability

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These gifts last only until an appointed time, when God will hold people accountable for gratitude and fulfilling their obligations toward them.
rows.anchor: A time is finally to come when God will hold him accountable for these favours

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning to fear what lies ahead and behind evokes being swallowed by the earth or struck by falling pieces from heaven.
rows.anchor: they are thrusted with the earth and pieces are thrown down on them from the heavens

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than heed this warning, the people evade it and demand a sign of punishment.
rows.anchor: instead of paying heed they show evasion and demand a sign for punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to the conditional particle is omitted because the context makes it obvious.
rows.anchor: The answer to the conditional particle اَذِإِ is suppressed here because of obvious contextual indications

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “from the heavens and the earth” is also elided after “before you and behind you”; Sūrah Sabā’ supplies a parallel wording.
rows.anchor: In Sūrah Sabā’, the words are:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their evasion and rejection have become so entrenched that signs from God fail to influence them.
rows.anchor: this evasion and rejection has got the better of them so much

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When urged to share God’s provision with the needy, disbelievers mock the duty, reasoning that God could have fed the poor if He had willed it and that helping them would displease Him.
rows.anchor: they reply that why should they spend on those whom God has deprived

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an leaves this foolish, callous argument unanswered because its absurdity needs no comment; it illustrates how corrupted hearts and intellects behave.
rows.anchor: It has completely ignored it because its foolishness and callousness so evident that no comment is required.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since they ignore God’s signs, they persistently demand to see the threatened punishment before believing its messengers.
rows.anchor: when these people do not pay heed to the verses of God and only continue

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single sudden blast will seize them while they argue, leaving them unable to make a will or return to their families.
rows.anchor: whilst they are entangled in these discussions, it will catch them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despair of God and bad assumptions about Him are major causes of polytheism and religious innovation.
rows.anchor: One of the biggest factors leading to polytheism and innovation is a person loosing hope in God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Distrusting God’s mercy leads polytheists to invent supposed favorites of God and seek their intercession to obtain forgiveness.
rows.anchor: a polytheist does not have trust in God’s mercy and forgiveness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who sinned and committed polytheism should seek forgiveness from God alone; He forgives servants who turn to Him sincerely.
rows.anchor: They should seek forgiveness from Him alone. He is very forgiving and merciful.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse addresses people who think not everyone can approach God or have their petitions accepted, and therefore seek intermediaries; this shows despair and a forbidden bad opinion of God.
rows.anchor: the addressees are in fact those people who are under the misconception that neither can every person access God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking mercy should turn wholly to God, sever other supports, repent, seek forgiveness, submit, and worship and obey Him alone.
rows.anchor: a person should totally turn to God while severing ties from other means and supports

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the torment could mean the Hereafter, context points to the worldly punishment of a messenger’s direct audience after truth is conclusively conveyed; afterward, faith and help are no longer possible.
rows.anchor: contextual indication shows that it refers to the torment which visits the direct addressees of a messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 55 elaborates the previous verse’s call to turn to God: the “best thing” is the Qur’an, called the “best word” in 39:23.
rows.anchor: the best word) in verse twenty three of this sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is God’s final and most complete Book.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ān is the final and most complete Book of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is protected from alteration.
rows.anchor: It is secure from any fragment of alteration.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It calls people to the natural religion and lacks the stern, harsh directives found in previous scriptures.
rows.anchor: It invites people to the natural religion and hence is free of the stern and harsh directives of the previous scriptures.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Arabs, the Qur’an’s lucid, eloquent Arabic is unmatched, and its Arabic revelation is a great divine favor to them.
rows.anchor: it is in very eloquent and lucid Arabic the very likes of which others are not able to produce

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its mutashābih and mathānī form doubles its benefit compared with other divine books, as discussed at 39:23.
rows.anchor: This Book was revealed as mutashābih and mathānī as a result of which its benefit doubled

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an calls Arabs to Abraham’s religion, a message already familiar to them.
rows.anchor: This Book invites people to the religion of the great forefather of the Arabs: Abraham

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given these qualities, people should wholeheartedly welcome and absorb the Qur’an; denying it brings an unimaginable punishment.
rows.anchor: people should whole-heartedly welcome it and absorb it in their minds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A governing noun (mudāf) is omitted before “an,” as in examples discussed in earlier sūrahs.
rows.anchor: A governing noun ( mud@āf) is suppressed before the word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has made these arrangements so the heedless will not regret their neglect at accountability: worldly pleasures distracted them from the Hereafter, and they mocked its reminders.
rows.anchor: lured away by the absorbing pleasures of this world they continued to remain oblivious of the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excuse that God would have guided them is thwarted because He has revealed guidance; those who evade it remain responsible for turning away.
rows.anchor: to thwart such excuses the Almighty has revealed His guidance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On seeing the torment, the person wishes to return to worldly life and become among those grateful to God.
rows.anchor: so that they could become among those grateful to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This rebuts the excuse in 39:57: God’s revelations came, but the people denied them, acted arrogantly, and remained disbelievers.
rows.anchor: God did reveal His verses to them for their guidance; but they rejected them, showed arrogance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides by teaching people and then leaves acceptance to their discretion rather than forcing guidance into their hearts.
rows.anchor: He makes arrangement to guide people by teaching them, and then leaves it to their discretion whether they accept it or not.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who falsely speak about God are those who commit polytheism by claiming He has partners.
rows.anchor: allude to polytheism. I have already explained this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They persisted in claiming partners for God without justification out of arrogance, and their faces will be blackened because of that arrogance.
rows.anchor: On the Day of Judgement, the faces of such people will be blackened because of their arrogance.
